demand.question: Lazy loading (cache-aside): how it works on a hit and on a miss; advantages (only requested data cached; node failure not fatal); disadvantages (miss penalty of three trips; stale data).
Write-through: how it works; advantages (data never stale); disadvantages (write penalty, missing data until written, cache churn); combine with lazy loading.
Time to live (TTL): what it does, why add it to every key except write-through keys, adding randomness (jitter) to TTLs; 'Russian doll' or short TTL for fast-changing data.
Types of database caching: database-integrated cache, local (application) cache, remote cache; why a remote shared cache suits a fleet of servers.
Evictions: what happens when cache memory is full; eviction policies (allkeys-lru, volatile-lru, volatile-ttl, noeviction, ...); the ElastiCache default maxmemory-policy; reserved memory.
